newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: FIREFIGHTERS SAVE 30-YEAR PROJECT
In Melbourne, firefighters saved a 30 year research project when fire destroyed part of a house at Brunswick last night.
Two people ran from the house in Carnarvon Street and raised the alarm when the blaze started just after nine o'clock.
Their life work -- a specialised dictionary SYRIC -- was saved.
It's believed the fire was started by a candle left burning in a bedroom.
AMERICAN TOURIST KILLED IN FREAK ACCIDENT
An American tourist has been killed in a freak accident at Walkerville near Wilson's Promontory early this morning.
The 56-year-old man died instantly when a tree fell onto a tent in which he was sleeping at a caravan park just after midnight.
His name has not been released.
Meanwhile the death of a pedestrian at Castella, north of Yarra Glen overnight has taken the Christmas holiday road toll in Victoria to 9
Police say the 30 year old man from St Kilda was struck and killed as he crossed the Melba Highway just after ten o'clock.
CYCLONE PHIL UPGRADED TO CATEGORY THREE
The Weather Bureau in Perth says Cyclone Phil could still pose some threat to coastal communities in north Western Australia, and has now been upgraded to a category three.
The cyclone is currently situated 450-kilometres north-west of Broome, and 560-kilometres north of Port Headland, moving slowly west at seven-kilometres an hour.
A cyclone watch is current for coastal communities between Wallal and Exmouth.
Senior Forecaster Len Van Burgel says the cyclone's longer term movement is expected to be west-south-west, which places it parallel with the north-west coast.
FAMILY TAX PACKAGE DESCRIBED AS UNWORKABLE
The Federal Government's Family Tax initiative is being described as unworkable and un-Australian by the National Tax and Accountants Association.
President, Ray Regan, says the requirement for separated parents to fill in log books as a record of the time they spend with their children is ridiculous.
He says more than 600-thousand families will lose, under the new scheme.
COMMISSION SAYS PRESSURE ILL-CONCEIVED
The Human Rights and Equal Opportunities Commission says pressure on the Federal Government to override the High Court decision in the Wik case is "ill-conceived and lamentable".
Commission President and former High Court Judge Sir Ronald Wilson, says the decision of the High Court that pastoral leases don't extinguish native title was very clear.
Sir Ronald says the push to legislate against the verdict could wreak havoc on the reconciliation process, and the legitimate aspirations of Indigenous Australians.
He says any further amendments to the Native Title Act should preserve the substance of indigenous rights.
Sir Ronald wants talks between government and indigenous leaders before any amendments are considered.
